trigger: the daily collector on a stock rpm-ostree host (/usr/local -> ../var/usrlocal), or one whose /usr/local is on NFS
classification_rationale: A constrained python read failed the whole installed_software cycle every day (ConstrainedPolicy::fail)
summary: A constrained python read failed the whole installed_software cycle every day (ConstrainedPolicy::fail). Owner ruling 2026-10-29: both var/usrlocal/bin as a covered alias of usr/local/bin (the var/opt/java precedent) and ConstrainedPolicy::drop_source for the python row (the SAM.2 hunks copied verbatim), so any remaining constraint withholds only the python rows and the cycle continues. Reported independently by unhappy-path. Fixed in the gate-fix: governance r1 commit.

classification_rationale: The in-product explainer said six in-process actions and its source table had no runtimes.python row, while the manual says seven
summary: The in-product explainer said six in-process actions and its source table had no runtimes.python row, while the manual says seven. Text only; reported by plugin-developer too. Fixed in the gate-fix: governance r1 commit.

summary: The hand-written Installed-software inventory row did not name runtimes.python or the python ecosystem. Fixed in the gate-fix: governance r1 commit.

trigger: a reader sizes the Windows walk
classification_rationale: README said the Windows walk is bounded to 4,096 rows; the budget is RowByteBudget{kMaxTagsVisited, kMaxRowBytes}, so 512 rows
summary: README said the Windows walk is bounded to 4,096 rows; the budget is RowByteBudget{kMaxTagsVisited, kMaxRowBytes}, so 512 rows. Fixed in the gate-fix: governance r1 commit.

summary: Stale lists: software_inventory_types.hpp ecosystem comment, the collector's six-table-actions retry comment, routed-concerns.md source list, runtimes meson.build header. rest_api_v1.cpp's ecosystem schema description was already stale before this branch and is left alone. classification_rationale: The runtimes routed-concern row named only the Linux mount guard and linux: tokens
summary: The runtimes routed-concern row named only the Linux mount guard and linux: tokens. Extended to the macOS getmntinfo_r_np snapshot and its tokens and to the Windows registry leg (no network concept, per-user hives never opened); invariants otherwise unchanged. trigger: a future edit copies a Guard (no copy exists today)
summary: The raw-HKEY Guard was copy-constructible. Given a two-argument constructor and a deleted copy constructor (copy assignment was already deleted by the reference member); a deleted copy alone would end aggregate initialisation. Fixed in the gate-fix: governance r1 commit.

trigger: an administrator-written PythonCore key with many over-long subkey names
classification_rationale: The name_too_long continue ran before the kMaxTagsVisited count, so over-long names did not count against the 512 cap
summary: The name_too_long continue ran before the kMaxTagsVisited count, so over-long names did not count against the 512 cap. The count now precedes it, with a FakeOps case. Fixed in the gate-fix: governance r1 commit.

classification_rationale: pythoncore_reg.txt and windows/provenance.txt were loaded by no test (owner rule: commit only fixtures a test loads)
summary: pythoncore_reg.txt and windows/provenance.txt were loaded by no test (owner rule: commit only fixtures a test loads). Deleted; the capture narrative goes in the PR body. docs/samples/windows.txt, which the readme gate loads, stays. Fixed in the gate-fix: governance r1 commit.

trigger: the same PythonCore tag without InstallPath in both registry views
classification_rationale: Intended: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Python is redirected under WOW64, so a record in each view is a separate registration and only a shared install path proves one install
summary: Intended: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Python is redirected under WOW64, so a record in each view is a separate registration and only a shared install path proves one install. Stated in a code comment at dedupe_python_rows; the server collapses same-version rows anyway. Fixed in the gate-fix: governance r1 commit.

trigger: a host whose only python3.<minor> in /usr/bin is a symlink (alternatives, a manual link)
classification_rationale: Accepted as designed: an alias entry is a listed silent case (routed-concern invariant 2) and every surveyed distro ships regular files
summary: Accepted as designed: an alias entry is a listed silent case (routed-concern invariant 2) and every surveyed distro ships regular files. README caveat 2 now names the Linux python3.<minor> link explicitly (caveats stay at five). Fixed in the gate-fix: governance r1 commit.

summary: Rejected: docs/os-capability-matrix.md:96 already says runtimes is Linux full for dotnet/jvm and constrained for python, and row 147 says the Linux python leg is declared constrained for that reason.

trigger: an administrator writes a framework Info.plist with the key inside a comment or nested dict
classification_rationale: Accepted: the first <key> match wins, the file is admin-writable only and every value is still gated (version shape; no '&' or control characters)
summary: Accepted: the first <key> match wins, the file is admin-writable only and every value is still gated (version shape; no '&' or control characters). Stated in the function comment. Fixed in the gate-fix: governance r1 commit.
